Area Forecast Discussion...UPDATED
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
504 AM PDT Thu Apr 2 2026

.SYNOPSIS...02/224 AM.

Cooler than normal conditions will continue through Thursday, with
significant warming Friday through Sunday. Gusty north winds on 
Thursday will be followed by a moderate to locally strong Santa
Ana wind event Friday through Saturday.

&&

.SHORT TERM (TDY-SAT)...02/1235 AM.

Brisk NW flow will continue over the area today. This flow will
enhance the Northwesterly winds generated by a onshore push to 
the east that will reach 6 mb by this afternoon. Wind gusts will 
reach advisory levels of 45 mph across the western portion of the 
SBA south coast today. By early afternoon 40 to 50 mph gust will 
develop across the western portion of the Antelope Vly and 
foothills. The NW flow will also bank clouds up against the north 
slope and create a chance of some showers through the day. Aside 
from the winds this morning will feature a mix of clouds and 
sunshine as the left over moisture from Tuesday's nights rain 
forms some areas of cloudiness, but these clouds should dissipate 
by the afternoon leaving mostly sunny skies in their wake. The 
csts/vlys will warm some today with the added sunshine and highs 
will end up in the mid 60s to lower 70s. The interior will see a 
decrease in temps as cool air moves in from the San Joaquin Vly. 
Most Max temps will end up 2 to 4 degrees blo normal.

Tonight will be all about the winds. The offshore push from the
north will quickly ramp up to about 5 mb while the 6 mb onshore
push to the east will rapidly switch to 5 mb offshore by dawn.
Advisory level wind gusts 45 to 55 mph will develop through the
I-5 corridor and the Santa Susanna mtns. After midnight advisory
level gusts will develop across the SBA mtns and the eastern
portion of the Santa Ynez Range.

Friday morning will dawn with a developing Santa Ana wind event
as well as NE wind event for the Central Coast. Due to the rapid
switch from onshore to offshore in the E/W gradient this event
will be at least a moderate event and has the potential to be a
strong event. Gusts of 45 to 55 mph are likely with this event
through the Santa Ana Wind Corridor (Roughly a 30 mile corridor
with a mid-line extending from the Santa Clarita Vly to Pt Mugu).
There is 40 percent chc that warning level (60+ mph gusts) will
occur across the mtn areas east of the Santa Clarita Vly, The
Santa Susanna's and the western portion of the Santa Monicas. Due
to this potential a high wind watch is in effect for those areas
for Friday. Aside from the winds sunny skies and rising hgts from
an incoming ridge will combine with the offshore flow and bring
and 8 to 12 degree warming trend to the csts and vlys. This
warming will bring back warmer than normal temps with highs
reaching the mid 70s to lower 80s.

Saturday will be similar to Friday. The gradients and upper
support will be a little weaker and the winds will be weaker but
some wind advisories will likely be necessary for gusts between 
35 and 50 mph in the morning. The ridge will peak and max temps 
will bump up anther 3 to 6 degrees, raising almost all max temps 
across the csts/vlys into the 80s.

.LONG TERM (SUN-WED)...02/224 AM.

The ridge will weaken some on Sunday. More importantly the
offshore flow will weaken dramatically and will only be around 1
mb. Offshore winds, if any, will not amount to much. The weaker
offshore push will allow for an earlier and stronger sea breeze
and this will cool the csts/vlys by 2 to 4 degrees. Continued
airmass warming will bring 1 or 2 degrees of warming to the
interior.

On Monday a trof will push the ridge to the east and hgts will
fall. The offshore flow turns onshore by 1 to 3 mb and this will 
lead to 5 to 10 degrees of cooling across the board. Despite this
cooling max temps will end up 3 to 6 degrees above normal across
the csts and vlys, but 6 to 12 degrees across the interior.

Mdl disagreement continues for on the upper level pattern on 
Tuesday and Wednesday. The GFS still has more of a troffing pattern
while the EC continues to favor ridging. Both mdls show onshore
flow through the period. The ensembles are now shifting their
focus a little more the GFS's way of thinking showing minimal
change in temps Tue and noticeable cooling on Wed.

Both AI mdls indicate dry conditions through at least the 15th of
the month. Both mdls continue to indicate continued above normal 
max temps.

&&

.AVIATION...02/1200Z.

At 0828Z at KLAX, there was no marine layer nor an inversion.

Overall, fair confidence in TAFs through 20Z. Cigs will shift 
between layers between 025 and 050 through 20Z. SCT conds are 
very likely after 20Z.

KLAX...Fair confidence in TAF. SCT-BKN conds will vary between 
025 and 050 through 20Z. Good confidence in SCT conds aft 20Z. No 
significant east wind component expected.

KBUR...Fair confidence in TAF. SCT-BKN conds will vary between 
025 and 050 through 20Z. Good confidence in SCT conds aft 20Z.

&&

.MARINE...02/224 AM.

Widespread strong Small Craft Advisory (SCA) winds are today 
across the majority of the coastal waters. A Gale Watch was is in
effect for low-end GALES across the Outer waters this afternoon 
and this evening tonight. Local gusts to 35 knots are also 
possible across western portions of the Santa Barbara Channel and 
the inner waters north of Point Sal.

Seas will build quickly today, peaking this evening. Seas could 
reach SCA levels (10-12) feet over the outer waters and inner 
waters north of Point Sal. Seas for the southern inner waters 
should peak around 4 to 7 feet. Wave heights should drop off 
rather quickly as winds shift to the northeast Friday morning.
